title: Why Are We Always Looking for Better Partners? | Juice Bros Pickleball
description:
🎙️ Have you ever looked around the courts and thought...

"I wish I had a better partner."

Let's be honest... most pickleball players have.

But here's the real question...

👉 Are you actually the better partner?

In this episode of the Juice Bros Pickleball Podcast, we dive into one of the biggest (and most uncomfortable) conversations in pickleball. Why are players always chasing stronger partners? Is loyalty overrated? Does playing with better players actually help you improve? Or are we all looking at the problem the wrong way?

We also kick off our brand-new segment, 🧃 The Juice Press, where we cover the latest stories from around the pickleball world, including PaddleTech's acquisition of Pickle, the growing trend of major paddle companies buying smaller brands, and why most recreational players don't really follow pro pickleball.

description:
Before pickleball, Dav was a gamer who had never competed in a sport in his life. No sports teams, no athletic identity, nothing. Then a health scare changed everything — and pickleball found him.

title: The Pickleball Plateau | Juice Bros Pickleball
description:
Why do so many pickleball players feel like their game stops improving?

In this episode of Juice Bros Pickleball, Adrian and I talk about something almost every player experiences at some point — the pickleball plateau.

You’re playing regularly, showing up to rec games, and getting plenty of court time… but somehow your game doesn’t seem to be getting better.

We break down some of the common reasons players plateau, including:
 • playing too many rec games and not enough drilling
 • repeating the same habits without intentional practice
 • playing the same opponents over and over
 • mental frustration when improvement slows

We also talk about what helped us personally push through plateaus and what players can do if they feel stuck in their pickleball journey.

If you’ve ever felt like your game isn’t progressing, this episode should feel very relatable.
